title: Rough idle or shaking when stopped
h1: Why does my car shake or idle rough when stopped?
metaDesc: Rough idle or shaking at a stop? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's a misfire, vacuum leak or engine mounts, how urgent it is, and what to tell your mechanic.
synonyms: car shakes in drive when stopped
intro: An engine that shakes at a stop is either running unevenly or passing normal vibration into the car through worn mounts. Warning lights and the way the shake changes with gear, A/C and temperature tell these apart quickly. Answer the questions below to find the most likely cause and how soon to act.
safety: If the check engine light is flashing, pull over safely and turn off the engine.
If the temperature gauge is in the red or you see steam, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the oil pressure light comes on, stop the engine as soon as it's safe.
If you smell raw fuel, pull over as soon as it's safe, turn off the engine and keep sparks and flames away.

q_warning.q: Do you see any of these warning signs on the dash?
q_warning.help: The check engine light is the amber engine-shaped symbol. The oil pressure light looks like a red oil can.

opts.a: The check engine light is flashing
The temperature gauge is high or in the red, or there's steam
The red oil pressure light is on
The check engine light is on steady
It also stumbles, jerks or feels weak when I accelerate
A hissing sound from the engine, or the idle speed goes up and down
It only shakes at idle and drives fine

q_no_light.help: Engine mounts are rubber blocks that hold the engine in place and soak up its vibration.

opts.a: Worse in Drive or Reverse at a stop, smoother in Park or Neutral
There's a clunk or jolt when I shift or accelerate
Worse when the A/C is on
Rough only when cold, and smooths out when warm
Rough and uneven all the time, even in Park

result.title: The engine may be misfiring badly, which can damage the catalytic converter
result.now: Pull over safely and turn off the engine. Have the car towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If the light stops flashing after a restart, the problem is still there. Get it checked before driving any distance.
If you see smoke or smell burning from under the car, get away from the car and call for help.
If the oil pressure light comes on or you hear knocking, keep the engine off and don't restart it.
result.why: A flashing check engine light usually means the engine is misfiring badly enough to send unburned fuel into the exhaust. That fuel can overheat the catalytic converter within minutes and ruin it, and the shaking itself means a cylinder isn't doing its share.

causes.name: Failed ignition coil or spark plug
causes.clues: A sudden, rhythmic shake at idle and when accelerating.

causes.name: Fuel injector not working
causes.clues: The misfire stays on one cylinder after the ignition parts check out.

causes.name: Mechanical engine problem
causes.clues: A ticking or knocking noise, or a recent overheat.
causes.against: Much less common than an ignition problem.

you: Note when the flashing started and whether the shaking was sudden.

result.title: The engine may be overheating. Stop before it causes damage
result.now: Pull over safely and turn off the engine. Don't open the radiator cap while it's hot. Have it towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If you see steam or coolant leaking, stay clear of the engine until it cools completely.
If the coolant was low and you top it up, still have the cooling system checked before driving. Running hot again can warp the cylinder head.
If the oil pressure light comes on or you hear knocking, don't restart the engine.
result.why: An engine that runs too hot can start to misfire and shake, and continued driving can damage the head gasket or the engine itself. A rough idle with high temperature is a sign to stop right away.

causes.name: Low coolant from a leak
causes.clues: A sweet smell, steam, or a puddle of green, orange or pink fluid.

causes.name: Cooling fan not working
causes.clues: It overheats mostly at idle or in traffic, and cools down on the highway.

causes.name: Head gasket failure
causes.clues: White exhaust smoke with a sweet smell, or coolant keeps disappearing.

you: Once the engine is completely cool, check the coolant level in the see-through reservoir.
Look for puddles under the front of the car.
shop: Combustion gas test for a head gasket leak

result.title: The engine may be low on oil or losing oil pressure
result.now: Turn off the engine as soon as it's safe. Check the oil level once it's parked on level ground. Don't run the engine again until the cause is found.
if: If the oil is very low, adding oil may turn the light off, but have it checked before driving. Find out where the oil went.
If the oil level is full and the light is still on, have it towed. The oil pump or a sensor may have failed.
result.why: Low oil pressure means the engine's moving parts aren't getting enough lubrication. Running it this way can destroy the engine within minutes, and a rough idle with this light can mean damage is already starting.

causes.name: Low oil level
causes.clues: An oil leak, burning oil, or a long time since the last oil change.

causes.name: Failing oil pump or clogged pickup
causes.clues: The oil level is fine but the light stays on, maybe with a ticking or knocking sound.

causes.name: Faulty oil pressure sensor
causes.clues: The light flickers, and the engine sounds normal.
causes.against: Don't assume it's the sensor until pressure is tested.

you: With the engine off and the car level, check the oil dipstick.

result.title: A misfire is a common cause, often from a worn ignition part
result.now: If the check engine light starts flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn off the engine. Otherwise: Have the engine scanned for codes within the next few days. Until then, keep trips short and avoid hard acceleration.
if: If the check engine light starts flashing, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the oil pressure light comes on, the temperature gauge climbs, or you smell raw fuel, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the engine stalls, especially while moving or at intersections, avoid driving until it's checked. When the engine dies, steering and braking take much more effort.
If the spark plugs are due by your maintenance schedule, mention it. They're a common cause, and a shop will usually confirm which cylinder is misfiring before replacing parts.
result.why: When one cylinder doesn't fire properly, the engine loses its smooth rhythm and shakes, especially at idle and when accelerating. A steady check engine light along with stumbling often points to a misfire, and leaving it can damage the catalytic converter over time.

causes.name: Worn spark plugs
causes.clues: The plugs haven't been changed in a long time, or it's worse when accelerating.

causes.name: Failing ignition coil or plug wire
causes.clues: A misfire on one cylinder, or worse in damp weather.

causes.name: Clogged or failing fuel injector
causes.clues: The misfire stays on one cylinder after the ignition parts are checked.

you: Check your records for the last spark plug change.
Many auto parts stores will read the codes for you.

result.title: Extra air leaking in or a dirty throttle is a common cause (vacuum leak or throttle body)
result.now: Book a check and ask for a code scan and a vacuum leak test. Mention that it's worst at idle.
if: If the engine stalls, especially while moving or at intersections, avoid driving until it's checked. When the engine dies, steering and braking take much more effort.
If the check engine light starts flashing, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the oil pressure light comes on, the temperature gauge climbs, or you smell raw fuel, pull over and turn off the engine.
result.why: At idle, the engine runs on a small, carefully measured amount of air. A cracked hose or leaking gasket lets in extra air the computer doesn't know about, which makes the idle shaky or hunt up and down. A dirty throttle body can cause a similar rough idle.

causes.name: Cracked vacuum hose or leaking intake gasket
causes.clues: A hissing sound with the engine running, or a lean code on a scan.

causes.name: Dirty throttle body or idle control fault
causes.clues: A low or uneven idle that may improve slightly when you touch the gas.

causes.name: Faulty PCV valve or hose
causes.clues: A whistle or hiss, or oil residue around the hose.

you: With the engine idling, listen carefully around the top of the engine for hissing.
Look for cracked or disconnected rubber hoses (keep hands clear of belts and fans).
shop: Code scan and fuel trim data

result.title: A fuel leak or a leaking injector is possible
result.now: If you're driving, pull over when it's safe. Turn off the engine and look for wet spots or dripping fuel under the car and around the engine. If you find any or the smell is strong, have it towed.
if: If you see fuel dripping, keep everyone away from the car and call for help.
If you can't find a leak and the smell is faint, still have it checked before driving. Fuel leaks are a fire risk.
result.why: A rough idle with a raw fuel smell can mean an injector is leaking or stuck open, flooding a cylinder, or that fuel is leaking outside the engine. Either way, fuel near a hot engine is a fire risk.

causes.name: Leaking or stuck-open fuel injector
causes.clues: A misfire on one cylinder, black smoke, or hard starting when warm.

causes.name: Leaking fuel line or fuel rail
causes.clues: A wet spot or drips under the car or on the engine.

causes.name: Engine running very rich
causes.clues: Black smoke and a fuel smell at the tailpipe, with poor fuel economy.

you: Look for wet spots or drips under the car. Don't smoke or use flames nearby.
shop: Code scan and fuel trim data

result.title: Worn engine or transmission mounts are a likely cause
result.now: Book an inspection of the engine and transmission mounts. Mention that it shakes more in Drive than in Park.
if: If you hear loud clunks when shifting or accelerating, or the engine visibly lurches, get it checked within a few days.
If a hard clunk is followed by a fuel or coolant smell, a leak, or a warning light, stop and have it checked before driving further. A badly broken mount can let the engine pull on hoses and wiring.
If the shake is the same in Park and Drive, the engine itself may be running rough instead.
result.why: Mounts are rubber blocks that hold the engine and soak up its normal vibration. When they crack or collapse, you can feel the engine through the car, mostly in gear at a stop where the engine is pulling against the brakes. A badly broken mount can let the engine move enough to strain hoses and wiring.

causes.name: Worn or collapsed engine mount
causes.clues: More shaking in Drive or Reverse than in Park, and a clunk when shifting.

causes.name: Worn transmission mount
causes.clues: A clunk or jolt when accelerating from a stop.

causes.name: Engine idling slightly rough
causes.clues: The shake is there in Park too, or the idle speed wanders.

you: Compare the shake in Park, Neutral and Drive with your foot firmly on the brake.
shop: Watch for engine movement while shifting with the brakes held
Code scan to rule out a misfire

result.title: The idle may be too low to handle the A/C load
result.now: Book a check when convenient and mention that the shake gets worse with the A/C on.
if: If the engine stalls when the A/C kicks on, get it checked within a few days, and avoid driving if it stalls while moving. Steering and braking get much heavier when the engine dies.
If the temperature gauge climbs with the A/C on, turn the A/C off, pull over and turn off the engine.
If it also shakes more in Drive than in Park, worn engine mounts may be adding to it.
result.why: The A/C compressor adds load to the engine. The engine computer should raise the idle slightly to make up for it. If the idle control is dirty or a mount is worn, you feel the engine labor and shake.

causes.name: Dirty throttle body or idle control fault
causes.clues: The idle drops noticeably when the A/C turns on.

causes.name: Worn engine mounts
causes.clues: The shake is also worse in Drive than in Park.

causes.name: A/C compressor problem
causes.clues: A grinding or rattling noise when the A/C turns on.

you: At a stop, switch the A/C on and off and watch whether the engine speed dips.
shop: Idle control and throttle body check

result.title: A cold-start rough idle often points to a sensor or carbon buildup
result.now: Book a check when convenient. Note the outside temperature and how long it takes to smooth out.
if: If the check engine light comes on or it starts running rough when warm too, get it checked within a few days.
If the check engine light starts flashing, pull over and turn off the engine.
If it stalls when cold, mention it. That makes it more urgent, and if it stalls while moving, avoid driving until it's checked.
result.why: A cold engine needs extra fuel and a slightly higher idle. If a temperature sensor gives the computer a wrong reading, or carbon has built up on the valves or injectors, the engine can run rough until it warms up.

causes.name: Faulty coolant temperature sensor
causes.clues: The temperature gauge acts oddly, or fuel economy has dropped.

causes.name: Carbon buildup or dirty injectors
causes.clues: A higher-mileage engine, especially a direct-injection one.

causes.name: Small vacuum leak
causes.clues: A hiss that's louder when cold, as rubber and gaskets shrink.

you: Note how long after a cold start the shake goes away.
shop: Code scan and live sensor data

result.title: The engine may be running unevenly at idle. A misfire or air leak is possible
result.now: If the check engine light starts flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn off the engine. Otherwise: Book a check and ask for a code scan, even with no warning light. Problems at idle often show up as stored data before the light comes on.
if: If the check engine light comes on or the car stumbles when accelerating, get it checked within a few days.
If the check engine light starts flashing, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the oil pressure light comes on, the temperature gauge climbs, or you smell raw fuel, pull over and turn off the engine.
result.why: A rough idle that's the same in Park and in gear usually comes from the engine itself rather than the mounts. Early ignition wear, a small vacuum leak or a dirty throttle body are common causes, and they're easiest to fix before they cause a misfire.

causes.name: Worn spark plugs or weak ignition coil
causes.clues: A rhythmic shake or stumble, and plugs that are due for a change.

causes.name: Vacuum leak
causes.clues: A hissing sound, or an idle speed that hunts up and down.

causes.name: Dirty throttle body
causes.clues: A low idle that improves slightly when you touch the gas.

you: Check your records for the last spark plug change.
Listen for hissing around the top of the engine while it idles.
shop: Code scan, misfire counts and fuel trim data

result.title: Get a code scan to narrow it down
result.now: Book a check and ask for a code scan. Note whether the shake changes in Park versus Drive and with the A/C on or off.
if: If the check engine light starts flashing or the temperature gauge rises, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the oil pressure light comes on or you smell raw fuel, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the engine stalls, especially while moving or at intersections, avoid driving until it's checked. When the engine dies, steering and braking take much more effort.
result.why: A rough idle can come from the engine running unevenly or from worn mounts letting normal vibration through. A code scan and a quick test in different gears can usually separate these quickly.

causes.name: Misfire from worn ignition parts
causes.clues: A rhythmic shake, or stumbling when accelerating.

causes.name: Vacuum leak or dirty throttle body
causes.clues: A hissing sound or a hunting idle speed.

causes.name: Worn engine mounts
causes.clues: Worse in Drive than in Park, or a clunk when shifting.

you: Record a short video at idle showing the engine speed on the tachometer, with sound.
